dgroup.description: Default group name to which new users are added if no group is specified.

home.description: Base directory path where user home directories will be created.

skel.description: Path to skeleton directory whose contents are copied to new user home directories.

first_uid.description: First numeric user ID (UID) to allocate for regular (non-system) users.

last_uid.description: Last numeric user ID (UID) to allocate for regular users.

first_gid.description: First group ID (GID) to allocate for regular user groups.

last_gid.description: Last group ID (GID) to allocate for regular user groups.

usergroups_enab.description: Whether to automatically create a group for each new user (named after the username).

mkhomedir.description: Whether to create home directories if missing using mkhomedir_helper (e.g., via PAM).

add_extra_groups.description: If enabled, add new users to supplementary groups listed in ADD_EXTRA_GROUPS_DEFAULT.

add_extra_groups_default.description: List of supplementary group names to add new users to when ADD_EXTRA_GROUPS is enabled.

default_home.description: If true, ensure the user’s home directory is created even if one already exists (e.g., on user re-add).

dir_mode.description: Octal permission mode used for newly created home directories (e.g., '0755').

setgid_home.description: If true, set the setgid bit on new home directories so new files inherit the group.

skeleton.description: Alias for SKEL — same meaning. Kept for backwards compatibility.

no_user_group.description: If true, skip creating per-user groups (overrides USERGROUPS_ENAB).

default.description: First UID for system accounts (users with UID < SYSTEM_UID_MIN are considered system users).

range_config.description: List of system UID/GID ranges used to distinguish system and regular accounts.
